07d315.title: Supabase @ :15421 — Attack Surface Map
07d315.content:
Reverse proxy (Kong 2.8.1) in front of self-hosted Supabase. Single origin http://host.docker.internal:15421.

## Service sub-origins/status
- `/rest/v1/` → 200 (PostgREST 16.1, OpenAPI/Swagger 2.0 spec, "standard public schema")
- `/auth/v1/` → 404 (service live via subpaths below; GoTrue v2.195.0)
- `/auth/v1/settings` → 200 (public auth config)
- `/auth/v1/health` → 200 (GoTrue v2.195.0)
- `/auth/v1/token` → 405 on GET (endpoint exists; POST expected)
- `/auth/v1/verify` → 400 (endpoint exists)
- `/storage/v1/` → 404; `/storage/v1/bucket` → 403 "Invalid Compact JWS" (Storage live, JWT-only)
- `/functions/v1/<*>` → 404 (NO Edge Functions exposed; all probed names 404)
- `/graphql/v1` → 404 (GraphQL NOT exposed)
- `/realtime/v1` → 404 (Realtime NOT on this origin)
- `/pg/*` → **postgres-meta FULLY EXPOSED, UNAUTHENTICATED** (see below)
- `/` , `/docs`, `/favicon.ico`, `/v1/` → 404

## postgres-meta (/pg/) — CRITICAL exposure
- `/pg/` 200 (name @supabase/postgres-meta 0.0.0-automated)
- `/pg/tables` 200 (229KB all tables)
- `/pg/columns` 200 (207KB all columns)
- `/pg/functions` 200 (233KB all function SQL defs)
- `/pg/roles` 200 (all DB roles: supabase_admin superuser, anon, authenticated, service_role, dashboard_user, supabase_etl_admin...)
- `/pg/policies` 200 (ALL RLS policies with definitions)
- `/pg/schemas`/`/pg/views`/`/pg/indexes`/`/pg/triggers`/`/pg/health`/`/pg/config` 200
- `/pg/query`,`/pg/secrets`,`/pg/version`,`/pg/extension` → 404

## Tables (11, all in OpenAPI; all exposed as CRUD in spec)
tenant, app_user, tenant_member, kategori, rak, buku, salinan, anggota, tarif_denda_history, peminjaman, peminjaman_detail

## RPC functions
- `get_user_tenants()` — POST /rest/v1/rpc/get_user_tenants, NO args, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path, SQL: `SELECT tenant_id FROM tenant_member WHERE user_id = auth.uid()`. Callable by anon (returns []). LINCHPIN of all tenant-scoped RLS policies.
- (pgbouncer.get_auth(p_usename) is SECURITY DEFINER returning username,password — internal, flag)

## RLS policy map (all PERMISSIVE, roles=[public], all check:null)
- tenant: Public read SELECT `true`  ← CROSS-TENANT public read
- app_user: read `(id=auth.uid())`; update `(id=auth.uid())`
- tenant_member: Members read `tenant_id IN get_user_tenants()`; Users read own `(user_id=auth.uid())`
- kategori: Public read `true` ← CROSS-TENANT; Members manage ALL `tenant_id IN get_user_tenants()`
- rak: Public read `true` ← CROSS-TENANT; Members manage ALL tenant-scoped
- buku: Public read undeleted `(dihapus=false)` ← CROSS-TENANT no tenant filter; Members read all; Members manage ALL tenant-scoped
- salinan: Public read salinan of undeleted buku (no tenant filter) ← CROSS-TENANT; + member policies
- anggota/tarif_denda_history/peminjaman/peminjaman_detail: Members read + Members manage ALL, tenant_id IN get_user_tenants()

## Auth config (/auth/v1/settings)
- disable_signup: FALSE (open self-registration)
- mailer_autoconfirm: TRUE (no email verify), phone_autoconfirm TRUE
- external OAuth: all disabled
- saml_enabled false; passkeys false

## Key observations for testers
1. REST table reads as anonymous return 401 code 42501 "permission denied for table X to anon" → anon role lacks table GRANTs; data access likely only via RPC. Feeds: self-register (signup open) to get authenticated JWT; check if authenticated has table grants.
2. Cross-tenant disclosure via public-read policies (tenant, kategori, rak, buku, salinan) if anon key obtainable.
3. get_user_tenants SECURITY DEFINER governs isolation; if compromised (search_path, ownership, or tenant_member writable), full tenant escape.
4. No INSERT policy on app_user/tenant_member in spec ⇒ member escalation may need auth signup path or mass-assignment.
5. No leaked anon/service keys observed on REST/OpenAPI/config endpoints. Storage requires valid JWT.
6. Edge Functions absent on this origin.

8fa339.title: Unauthenticated postgres-meta exposure → full DB control
8fa339.content:
Headline finding on http://host.docker.internal:15421 (Kong gateway in front of self-hosted Supabase):

The postgres-meta service is exposed unauthenticated at /pg/*. Verified reachability matrix:
- GET /pg/tables (228KB), /pg/columns (206KB), /pg/functions (233KB), /pg/roles, /pg/policies (24 policies), /pg/schemas, /pg/views, /pg/indexes, /pg/triggers, /pg/config, /pg/health, /pg/column-privileges, /pg/table-privileges → ALL 200 unauthenticated
- POST /pg/query → 200, EXECUTES ARBITRARY SQL unauthenticated as postgres role (rolcreaterole=true, rolcreatedb=true, can_bypass_rls=true)
- POST /pg/tables → 200, CREATES TABLES unauthenticated (created + dropped marker table zz_pentest_marker)

CRITICAL proven impact via POST /pg/query:
- Read auth.users: 5 users' emails + bcrypt password hashes
- INSERT into tenant + kategori (FK chain), read back, DELETE → full write chain proven
- DROP TABLE public.zz_pentest_marker proven
- RLS completely bypassable (postgres can_bypass_rls)
- postgres is NOT superuser (rolsuper=false) and pg_read_file denied → no direct file read/RCE, but full DB data read/write + role/db creation

REST API layer is properly gated: all 11 /rest/v1/<table> return 401 (42501 anon-permission-denied); get_user_tenants RPC returns []. So postgres-meta completely nullifies the app's access control.

Other: /auth/v1/settings 200 (open signup), /rest/v1/ OpenAPI 41KB exposed, storage JWT-gated (403).

All test artifacts cleaned up (marker table dropped, all inserted rows deleted, tables restored to original 11).

838f37.title: SQLi testing conclusive — no injection in PostgREST params
838f37.content:
Extensive SQLi testing of PostgREST at host.docker.internal:15421 is CONCLUSIVE: **no working SQL injection** in query parameters.

Root cause of non-reachability:
1. **Tables gated at permission layer**: All 11 public tables (tenant, app_user, tenant_member, kategori, rak, buku, salinan, anggota, tarif_denda_history, peminjaman, peminjaman_detail) grant `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` ONLY `MAINTAIN`/`REFERENCES`/`TRIGGER`/`TRUNCATE` — NO SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Every table read/write returns 401/403 (PGRST/42501) BEFORE PostgREST builds SQL. Verified via /pg/table-privileges and live 401/403 probes.
2. **Single RPC `get_user_tenants` (SECURITY DEFINER, lang=sql, SETOF uuid) takes NO arguments** — only public function in schema. Returns `[]`. Nothing injectable.
3. **PostgREST 16.1 parser rejects standard SQLi syntax** in select/order/columns: `(`, `;`, `::`, `+`, `count()`, embedded-resource tricks → PGRST100/PGRST108/PGRST123 parser errors, never reaching SQL.

Timing validation (airtight): `select=(select pg_sleep(3))` and variants on RPC return in 0.006-0.026s — no pg_sleep executes. No timing channel exists.

Write-path vectors (`columns=`, `on_conflict=`, POST/PATCH body) also gated: on_conflict POST → 403 permission, columns= → PGRST100 parser error, PATCH/DELETE with id → 22P02 uuid error before SQL.

**No vulnerability to report** — nothing has a SQL discriminator. Do NOT file a SQLi report.

ADJACENT FINDING (NOT SQLi, belongs to info-disclosure/access-control agents): `/pg/*` @supabase/postgres-meta is exposed unauthenticated, returning /pg/tables (228KB schema), /pg/roles (role list incl. superuser flags), /pg/functions (all function signatures), /pg/table-privileges, /pg/config. `/pg/run` (raw SQL executor) = 404. This is an unauthorized DB-metadata disclosure / access-control issue. Agent 13ae2461 (Unauthenticated Access & Info Disclosure) and 2df9d597 (BOLA) are covering this — coordinate with them, do not duplicate.

82a274.title: BOLA/tenant-isolation testing conclusive — REST layer fully gated, no cross-tenant vector
82a274.content:
BOLA & tenant-isolation testing on http://host.docker.internal:15421 is CONCLUSIVE: **no cross-tenant IDOR/BOLA via the REST API** because the DML/GRANT layer fully gates every public table.

Method:
1. Registered 2 fresh users via open signup (mailer_autoconfirm): userA `usera_bola@test.com` (id 09215a42-f32c-426d-9a12-6af7cd4ce79d) and userB `userb_bola@test.com` (id 8492cb5a-63d0-4914-84e1-5ba9c35ec5c1). Both logged in via grant_type=password → authenticated JWTs.
2. `POST /rest/v1/rpc/get_user_tenants` (SECURITY DEFINER, no args) → `[]` for userA, userB, and anon. No leak; no args to inject.
3. Authenticated GET on all 11 tables (tenant, app_user, tenant_member, kategori, rak, buku, salinan, anggota, tarif_denda_history, peminjaman, peminjaman_detail) → ALL 403 `42501 permission denied for table`. anon → 401. Even the supposedly "public read `true`" tables (tenant, kategori, rak, buku, salinan) are denied.

Root cause of non-exploitability (verified via /pg/table-privileges): for every public table, roles `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` hold ONLY TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER/MAINTAIN — NO SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. `postgres` alone has full DML. RLS policies (TO `public`) thus never take effect for REST roles; PostgREST returns 42501 before RLS/authz is even applied. The RLS policy design itself is reasonable (Members scoped via `tenant_id IN get_user_tenants()`, Users own-profile via `id=auth.uid()`); it is simply never reachable.

Membership-escalation (POST /rest/v1/tenant_member with userB's tenant_id) is also blocked: no INSERT grant → 403.

Conclusion: no independent cross-tenant BOLA/IDOR vulnerability exists in the REST layer. The only way any client reaches cross-tenant/any-tenant data is via the exposed postgres-meta `/pg/*` service (postgres role, bypasses RLS), which is ALREADY reported as vuln-0001 (critical, unauthenticated arbitrary SQL execution / full DB control). Any BOLA finding here would be a duplicate manifestation of that same root cause. Do NOT file a separate BOLA report.

a497e8.title: Auth, Mass Assignment & RPC findings — matrix + 2 filed reports
a497e8.content:
Scope: http://host.docker.internal:15421 (Kong, GoTrue 2.195, PostgREST 16.1, Storage).

FILED:
- vuln-0002 CRITICAL (9.8): Default/guessable JWT_SECRET `super-secret-jwt-token-with-at-least-32-characters-long` lets anyone forge an HS256 service_role JWT. Verified: GET /auth/v1/admin/users -> 200 full user list (15 accounts); PUT /auth/v1/admin/users/<id> {"password":"..."} -> 200 reset; login as victim with attacker password -> 200 (full account takeover). PostgREST also accepts forged service_role (runs queries as service_role, RLS-bypass), postgres role gets "permission denied to set role". Root cause CWE-798. Fix: rotate JWT_SECRET to high-entropy across all services.
- vuln-0003 MEDIUM (6.5): Refresh token rotation rotates (rt0->rt1) but old rt0 stays valid; replays return 200 + fresh access token indefinitely; only global logout invalidates (400 after logout). No reuse detection. CWE-613.

CONFIRMED NEGATIVES (do NOT re-file):
- Mass assignment: PostgREST has NO INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT grant for authenticated (nor service_role). GET/POST/PATCH on ALL 11 tables (tenant, app_user, tenant_member, kategori, rak, buku, salinan, anggota, tarif_denda_history, peminjaman, peminjaman_detail) -> 403 42501 permission denied. POST tenant_member (add self as owner) -> 403. PATCH app_user own row -> 403. No write escalation via PostgREST.
- RPC abuse: only `get_user_tenants` (SECURITY DEFINER, SETOF uuid, no args). Passing body/url params -> 404 PGRST202. select/order injection rejected (PGRST100/PGRST200). Returns [] for non-member. No SQLi, no mutation.
- Signup claim injection: GoTrue strips app_metadata (always overwritten to provider/providers), forces JWT role=authenticated regardless of data/app_metadata/role input. No escalation via signup.
- Storage: JWT-gated. anon -> 403 Invalid Compact JWS. auth can GET bucket -> [] (no buckets). POST bucket -> 403 RLS violation. Object paths -> 404 NoSuchBucket. No buckets on this origin.
- User enum via signup: existing email -> 422 user_already_exists, new -> 200 (true but low; informational).

Test users created for this work: authtest_a@example.com, authtest_b@example.com, inj1-5/injA-D. Password reset ATO demo was reverted (password restored to TestPass123!).
